questions.question: Is a load that is placed on the roof of your vehicle allowed to touch the road surface?

options.text: Only if you drive a bakkie

questions.explanation: A load may not come into contact with the road surface; it would be a hazard to you and to other road users.

questions.question: Are you allowed to have a load that exceeds 3 metres in height from the ground?

options.text: No, 3 metres is the max height allowed

questions.explanation: 3 metres is not the limit. The overall height of a vehicle with its load may not exceed 4,3 metres measured from the ground.

questions.question: Can you have a load that exceeds 4.3 metres in height from the ground?
questions.explanation: The overall height of a vehicle with its load, measured from the ground, may not exceed 4,3 metres (4,65 metres for a double-deck bus).

questions.question: Which of the following is true?

options.text: The load on your vehicle must not exceed half the height of your vehicle
Hatchbacks are not allowed to carry a load

questions.explanation: Goods on the roof of a motor car may not be higher than half the height of the car. Hatchbacks are allowed to carry a load, so B (and therefore C) is wrong.

questions.question: In terms of a light motor vehicle, what is the maximum width that your load is not allowed to exceed?
questions.explanation: For a light motor vehicle the maximum width of the load is 2,5 metres. A load that sticks out to the side must also be marked with red flags.

questions.question: In terms of a goods vehicle that weighs more than 12000 kg, what is the maximum width that your load is not allowed to exceed?
questions.explanation: For a goods vehicle of more than 12 000 kg the maximum width of the load is 2,6 metres.

questions.question: What is the furthest that a load may project to the front of the vehicle?
questions.explanation: A load may not project more than 300 millimetres beyond the front of the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the furthest that a load may project to the rear of the vehicle?
questions.explanation: A load may not project more than 1,8 metres beyond the rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a blind spot check?

options.text: To help you pass your driver's licence test
To ensure there are no vehicles or obstacles in areas not visible in your mirrors before changing lanes
Checking your blindspot is not important when on the public road

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes you must be sure the lane is clear, including areas your mirrors cannot show.

questions.question: What are the first two things you must do if your vehicle breaks down on a public road?

options.text: Stop your vehicle on the right lane and step out of your vehicle
Phone your boss and inform him that you will be late for work
Move off the road if possible and switch on your hazard lights

questions.explanation: Move your vehicle off the road if possible and switch on your hazard lights so that other road users can see it. Never stop in the right (fast) lane.

questions.question: What is the penalty for driving without a valid learner's or driver's licence?

options.text: You are allowed to drive on a public road without your learner's or driver's licence

questions.explanation: Driving without a valid learner's or driver's licence can result in a fine or imprisonment. A learner driver must also be accompanied by a licensed driver.

questions.question: What is the minimum legal tread depth for a car's tires?
questions.explanation: The minimum legal tread depth is 1 mm.

questions.question: What does a red circle around a number on a speed limit sign mean?

options.text: It indicates the minimum speed limit
It indicates the maximum speed limit

questions.explanation: A number in a red circle on a speed limit sign indicates the maximum speed limit.

questions.question: Who has the right of way at a four-way stop?

options.text: The vehicle that stops first, or if two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the one to the right
The person with the faster vehicle
Everyone should leave at the same time

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop the vehicle that stopped first moves off first.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a yellow line on the left side of the road?

options.text: It indicates that you are allowed to park here to have a smoke break
It marks the edge of the road and separates the emergency lane from the main road

questions.explanation: The yellow line on the left marks the edge of the road and separates the emergency lane (shoulder) from the main road.

questions.question: How far from a pedestrian crossing are you allowed to park?
questions.explanation: You are not allowed to park within 9 metres of a pedestrian crossing.

questions.question: What must you do when approaching a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Treat it as a stop sign; stop and proceed when safe
Don't bother stopping as it's not a solid red light
Stop and don't leave until a traffic officer instructs you to do so

questions.explanation: A flashing red traffic light means you must stop and may carry on when it is safe, as at a stop sign.

questions.question: When is it illegal to overtake another vehicle?

options.text: If you drive a slow vehicle
On a blind rise, curve, or when there's a solid white line

questions.explanation: You may not overtake on a blind rise or curve, or where there is a solid white line.

questions.question: What does a yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Prepare to stop if it's safe to do so

questions.explanation: A yellow (amber) light means you must stop, unless you cannot do so safely.

questions.question: What does a yield sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and give the right of way to other traffic

questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down and give right of way to other traffic; stop only if there is traffic in your way.
